messages.subject: Problems with legends (labeling and order)
parts:
Dear ggplot2-expeRts,

here is an example (questions below):

library(ggplot2)
set.seed(1)

df <- data.frame(x=rep(2000:2011, 3), group=rep(c("low", "middle",
"high"), each=12),
y=rep(2000:2011, 3)+100*runif(3*12))

qplot(x, y, data=df, color=group, geom="line")
## Okay, the legend has title "group" and entries "low", "middle",
"high".
## In order to get a different legend title with different entry
labels, create
## a new data.frame (is this the best way to do it?)

df. <- df
df.[,2] <- "My legend title"
levels(df.[,2]) <- c("low; 1", "middle; 2", "high; 3")
qplot(x, y, data=df., color="My legend title", geom="line")
## It's clear that this does not work since "My legend title" is a
character string.
## How can I fix this? (The legend title should also contain plotmath
commands).
## And as a final question, is there a way to change the order in
which the legend
## entries are displayed in the first plot (so for example, to "low",
"middle", "high")

Cheers,

Marius

messages.author: affa918ed63b6275
messages.subject: Re: Problems with legends (labeling and order)
parts:
hi

1. use backquote (``) to specify atypical variable name.
2. reorder the levels of factor.

here is an example:

df2 <- df
names(df2)[2] <- "My legend title"

## probably you need sort the levels of factor
# levels(df2[,2]) <- c("low; 1", "middle; 2", "high; 3")
levels(df2[,2]) <- sort(c("low; 1", "middle; 2", "high; 3") )

# use backquote `` to specify atypical variable name
qplot(x, y, data=df2, color=`My legend title`, geom="line")

# then, re-order the factor
df2[,2] <- factor(df2[,2], c("low; 1", "middle; 2", "high; 3") )
qplot(x, y, data=df2, color=`My legend title`, geom="line")

--

messages.subject: Re: Problems with legends (labeling and order)
parts:
Dear Kohske,

thanks a ton! I originally tried to used backquotes but it did not work. The reason was that I also added lines to the plot (with geom_line) and the data frame for that did contain the original name "group" instead of the new one "My legend title". So I had to change the name there, too, and then it worked.
Since I am new to ggplot2 and try to learn "good practices", is this really the best way to do it? If you add a lot of things to a plot (based on different data frames), then it requires to change the name in the different data frames. But I guess one should maybe first build a "good" data frame containing all the information before plotting...

Cheers,

Marius

Perhaps, case-by-case.
The meaning of "best" also depends on the context, e.g., elegant, fast, easy.
If you provide a concrete example, probably someone can suggest good
(not necessarily best) ways to plot it.

From my own experience, it is preferable to prepare a good data frame
before plotting.
Hadley have kindly created tools to do such work - plyr and reshape packages.

messages.author: 05f1cc3d29047e11
messages.subject: Re: Problems with legends (labeling and order)
parts: > Since I am new to ggplot2 and try to learn "good practices", is this really the best way to do it? If you add a lot of things to a plot (based on different data frames), then it requires to change the name in the different data frames. But I guess one should maybe first build a "good" data frame containing all the information before plotting...

You just have to use scale_colour_xxx('"My legend title"'), or
scale_fill_xxx() depending whether you use colour= or fill=

eg. qplot(x, y, data=df, color=group, geom="line") +
scale_colour_hue('My legend title', labels=c('low','medium','high',
breaks=1:3)

I would add my two cents by mentioning that your data frame contains
the data, whereas ggplot will take care of how you display your data.
To add a column just for changing labels doesn't seem like a 'good
practice' to me...
As a newbie myself, I haven't found a way to re-order the items
displayed other than re-ordering your factor in your dataframe. I
guess this is because your factors are tied to your data structure, as
opposed to the labelling you will use to describe them.

Hope this helps,
JP
